authors.bio: Phil Tudor is a principal engineer at BBC Research & Development, London, U.K. He read electrical and information sciences at Cambridge University. Tudor's technical background includes software engineering, video compression algorithm development, MPEG standardization, metadata interoperability and the development of AAF and MXF standard file formats for use in tapeless production. — Tudor is responsible for R&D projects in the areas of production tools, formats, workflow, media management and wide area production. He chairs the SMPTE 30MR Technology Committee on Metadata & Registers and is a board member of the Advanced Media Workflow Association. Tudor is a SMPTE fellow, a Chartered Engineer and a member of the Institution of Engineering Technology.
authors.name: Phil Tudor

authors.bio: Paul Treleaven obtained a First Class Honours degree in electrical engineering from Imperial College, London in 1972. He started his career in broadcast engineering with BBC Designs Department. His work included design of the interpolation system for the BBC's ‘ACE’ four-field standards converter. In 1979, Treleaven co-founded Avitel, a company designing and manufacturing video, audio and timecode distribution and processing equipment. He continued with Avitel as Technical Director until 2001. — Treleaven is a member of the International Association of Broadcasting Manufacturers' Technical Task Group, representing the IABM at SMPTE and AES standards meetings and ABU technology committee meetings. He is also a member of the UK's National Standards Body for IEC TC100. Treleaven has served as SMPTE International Region Governor and is a SMPTE Fellow. He is currently co-chair of the SMPTE Technology Committee on Metadata and Registers and has Chaired other SMPTE standards groups.
authors.name: Paul Treleaven
